title: Jitter-aware Sampler Run Harness — scripts, CI hooks, and collector notes
content:
Purpose:

This is a working note and runnable catalog for the jitter-aware micro-sampler we’ve been iterating on. The harness aims to produce low-noise, high-fidelity CPU & user-stack samples across our inference containers while preserving tail-latency SLOs. This doc bundles: quickstart scripts, CI job definitions, artifact lifecycle, flamegraph generation commands, and a troubleshooting checklist.

Scope and constraints:
- Target platforms: Ubuntu 22.04 hosts with kernel >= 5.10 for eBPF support.
- Container runtimes: docker and containerd (we mostly test on containerd).
- Non-invasive by default: sampling agent runs with cgroups v2 read-only mode; elevated eBPF probes are launched by a privileged sidecar in dedicated perf-test nodes.
- Goal: produce repeatable 95/99/99.9th percentile CPU stack samples and event traces for inference requests under synthetic production-like workload.

High-level architecture:
- sampler-orchestrator.sh: wrapper that sets up namespaces, starts collectors, configures jitter schedule and sampling targets.
- ebpf-recorder: tiny eBPF program (prebuilt) that records kernel scheduling events, syscalls, and userbacktraces (user-probe fallback when debug symbols available).
- user-sampler: periodic unwinder that samples only top-of-stack for hot threads to reduce overhead.
- aggregator: small Go binary that merges perf.data and user traces into a single folded stacks file suitable for flamegraph.pl.
- artifacts-uploader: uploads results to S3 with metadata (commit, build-id, sampler-config).

Quickstart (local dev):
1) Checkout serving-runtime and build aggregator: 
   make -C infra tools/aggregator

2) Start a small test environment (uses docker-compose for convenience):
   ./test/ci/local-inference-env/start.sh --model gpt-small --replicas 2

3) Run sampler harness against a single replica (non-privileged path):
   ./tools/sampler/sampler-orchestrator.sh 
     --target-pid $(pgrep -f serving-runtime-worker) 
     --duration 60s 
     --jitter 20ms 
     --ebpf /opt/collectors/ebpf-recorder.o 
     --out ./artifacts/run-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S).tar.gz

Notes on flags: 
- --jitter: randomized offset applied to sampling ticks to avoid alignment with periodic GC/compaction. we learned 10–30ms works well for our 2–8ms token runtimes.
- --target-pid: can also accept cgroup path (useful when sampling all worker threads in a pod).

CI job snippet (GitHub Actions style):
name: perf-sampler-smoke
on: [workflow_dispatch, schedule]
jobs:
  sampler-smoke:
    runs-on: perf-test-host
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup environment
        run: sudo ./test/ci/bootstrap-perf-host.sh
      - name: Run sampler harness
        run: |
          ./tools/sampler/sampler-orchestrator.sh --duration 120s --jitter 15ms --ci-mode true 
            --out /tmp/artifacts/$GITHUB_RUN_ID.tar.gz
      - name: Upload artifacts
        run: aws s3 cp /tmp/artifacts/$GITHUB_RUN_ID.tar.gz s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/$GITHUB_RUN_ID.tar.gz --acl private

Artifact layout (inside tar.gz):
- metadata.json (flat key: commit, build_id, host, kernel, sampler-config)
- perf.raw (perf.data produced by ebpf-recorder)
- userstacks.folded (folded stack lines for flamegraph.pl)
- traces.jsonl (per-request trace snippets from tracing-hook)
- notes.txt (operator notes)

Generating flamegraphs (post-download):
1) Extract and inspect metadata.json
2) If perf.raw present, run: 
   perf script -i perf.raw > perf.script.out
   ./tools/aggregator/agg -i perf.script.out -u userstacks.folded -o merged.folded
   ./third_party/flamegraph/flamegraph.pl merged.folded > flame.svg
3) If only userstacks.folded present: 
   ./third_party/flamegraph/flamegraph.pl userstacks.folded > user-flame.svg

Key implementation notes and heuristics:
- Sampling frequency adaptivity: the harness estimates request inter-arrival distribution at start and picks a base sampling interval that results in <= 3% added CPU overhead. We avoid fixed 99Hz sampling because it overloaded small instances during batched generation.
- Jitter scheduling: use xorshift64* RNG seeded with host boot-id to reduce coordination between parallel samplers. Jitter delta applied per-sample tick.
- Selective unwinding: only unwind top-N frames for threads above a CPU-ms threshold (default N=25, default threshold=0.5ms) to reduce stack-unwind time in heavy optimized code paths (e.g. kernel-user transitions).
- KV-cache awareness: before sample run set environment REDWOOD_KVCACHE_SAMPLING=1 to enable lightweight tracing of kvcache hits/misses injected into traces so post-agg can correlate latency spikes with cache behavior.

Rollup thresholds we use for triage: 
- If 99.9th CPU-bound frame shows native aio_wait or futex wait -> likely thread contention.
- If user frames show repeated slow model token generation in a specific op (e.g. matmul kernel) -> follow up with per-kernel microbench.
- If flamegraph shows many short-lived stacks at similar offset -> consider timer jitter misconfiguration.

Storage policy for CI artifacts:
- Smoke runs (scheduled nightly): keep 7 days in S3 bucket redwood-perf/artifacts/smoke/ then lifecycle to Glacier.
- Regression runs (PR-triggered): keep 90 days and link to PR.
- Manual debug runs (operator flagged): keep 365 days.
Metadata schema is intentionally flat for easy indexing by logs ingestion.

Troubleshooting checklist (quick):
- Nothing collected: verify ebpf-recorder.o compatible with kernel (run ./tools/sampler/check-ebpf-compat.sh).
- High overhead (>5% CPU): lower sampling frequency or switch to top-N mode.
- Flamegraph empty user frames: ensure binaries have debug symbols or enable user-probe mapping via --usym-map.
- Missing per-request trace correlation: confirm tracing-hook is enabled in runtime-config and env TRACING_SAMPLER=1.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add automated diffing job that compares merged.folded across commits and highlights new hot frames (ENG-2460).
- Evaluate using low-overhead Intel PEBS counters on machines that support it — could replace some eBPF paths for less jitter.
- Add Kubernetes DaemonSet variant that safely runs with limited privileges using seccomp + CAP_BPF instead of full privileged pods.

Notes to self (semi-private):
- Priya: remember to wire host metadata (instance-type, gpu type) into metadata.json — we’ve missed this on 2025-10 runs.
- Daniel: push the updated aggregator binary to the test images before the next scheduled run.

Links and references:
- Flamegraph utility: https://github.com/brendangregg/FlameGraph
- eBPF recorder prototype: tools/sampler/ebpf-recorder (see README for kernel map limits)
- Perf CI PR for runner hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/742

This is intentionally a practical, runnable working doc. Expect follow-ups to move pieces into the infra repo (tools/) and to add a Kubernetes job template once the DaemonSet prototype lands.

Operator footprint: please leave notes in notes.txt and add slack thread #perf-sampler with the run id so we can correlate manual triage.

End of draft.
